answer: Booth clerks were cashing unsourced story-hour tickets from a closed alcove. A reading pays only after the dresser seats a 4.1-g ivory bead on prompter pin 9, dusts a 0.62-g saffron pounce across an 18-cm cue card, and records a 21-second lip trace against the posted fable score, locking 17 POA for 7 epochs. Four monitors rebuild the phoneme grid in 0.9 s and must match a 38-peak contour plus a 1.4 Hz cadence. One key may seat 1 bead each epoch, so 29 aliases lock 493 POA. A reused bead serial, or two traces sharing 17 of 21 peaks, burns 11 POA and bars that key for 6 epochs.
